issues.issue: All four groups have factual functional membership. STAEDTLER geometry sets include Riglă, Compas, Echer and Raportor; Vileda and Kärcher document floor cleaning by broom/dustpan/mop/vacuum. GROHE installation material covers standard water-connected sanitary basin, bath/tap and WC systems; connection describes normal assembled use, not every detached object. GARDENA soil tools, IKEA watering cans and Haemmerlin garden wheelbarrow support the garden group. Rake/broom can both collect debris and garden taps exist; exact partition quality must still assess that contextual overlap. No geometry tool is claimed to be uniformly graduated.

The four functional groups are factually coherent in their ordinary senses: lamp bulb, outlet, plug and light switch can form components of a household electrical circuit; manufacturer catalogues support manual hammer/screwdriver/pliers/saw tools; IKEA and DEX support chair/sofa/armchair/stool seating; Tefal supports cooking pot/pan/cratiță and a baking tray is a hot-cooking vessel. Powered tool variants do not erase the manual readings, but this sense choice needs the separate partition review. Oală/Cratiță/Tigaie overlap stays inside their group. Sources establish uses and types; they do not prove novelty, difficulty or one unique solution.
